status: draft — issue #509, epic #507; split by issue #518 (ADR-0039); read by scripts/contracts/contract.sh and the module's command. Format: docs/records/design-reviews/io-contract-modules.md > 5.
goal: The branch on the remote at the last commit of the range the build made, with each sub-repo the invocation names pushed and its pointer set, and — unless the invocation says pull_request none — a draft pull request open for each, on the base, whose body lets the operator decide on it.

base.note: the branch the pull request is to merge into; not given, the remote's default branch

pull_request.note: none: the branches are pushed and no pull request is opened or updated; not given, open

timeout.note: the run's bound in seconds; not given, 900. Reaching it ends the run with its failure output

integration.note: given, the body states how the change was shown working above its own tests

tool_requests.note: Besides the criteria, the PR body owes the operator the tool requests of every run (§5.3) and the recommendations deferred or separated. Each path is one run's tool-requests.json.

deferred.note: a JSON array of the recommendations deferred or separated, each {subject, finding, disposition}: the disposition is the issue that takes it (#<n>, or <owner>/<repo>#<n>) or the gap stated in one line

sub_repos.note: a JSON array of the sub-repos to deliver, each {path, pointer}: path the sub-repo's directory in the host; each is pushed and, unless pull_request is none, gets its pull request; pointer false leaves the host's pointer where it is (not given, true). A changed sub-repo not named is not pushed, and the output names it

delivered.note: {pushed: [{repo, branch, head, path}], pull_requests: [{pr: <owner>/<name>#<N>, url, head, path, opened}], pointers: [{path, commit}], not_delivered: [{path, why}]} — opened true for a pull request this run opened; the review's pr is an entry's pr

checks.note: each open at the head the entry names, and a draft when this run opened it

failure.note: Written instead of the expected output when the run cannot reach it, or reaches its timeout: what the run did, what it observed, and why it did not reach the expected output — an input it needed and was not given named as such. check-out then writes `failed` (docs/units/delivery.md > What every delivery module owes).
